pr_title: usb: cdc_acm: Fix tx false data drop logging
pr_body:
Fixes #75988

cdc_acm_fifo_fill() logged warnings about dropped data when they in fact just couldn't be sent (due to connection of filled buffer). Not being able to send (all) data is a valid behaviour and data isn't dropped. Return value shows how many data was accepted (which can be zero).

Logging will now instead only inform data can't be sent due to the respective issue (connection / buffer full).

issue_context.title: usb: cdc_acm.c Logging shows false data drop warning
issue_context.body:
Logging error in CDC ACM:

In cdc_acm_fifo_fill() :
```
if (wrote < len) {
	LOG_WRN("Ring buffer full, drop %zd bytes", len - wrote);
}
```

Wrote is given as return value. Wrote being smaller than len is totally fine. The data doesn't get dropped and can be sent later.
It looks like a copy paste from the RX function cdc_acm_read_cb() (where it is correct as received data needs to be buffered or gets dropped).

Impact is low as it only gives a false warning when logging. Also it needs big chunks of data to be sent to fill the buffer.

Environment:
Xubuntu Linux
Zephyr SDK
zephyr commit f6600040e41114b8737dee5d6ea8415e417434c8

review_comments: See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/76171#discussion_r1687022631 for a discussion on why checking for suspended here might not be the best idea (it leads to autosuspend issues if device support Remote Wakeup).

Putting `Fixes issue #75988` in the commit message is useless. The correct way is to write `Fixes #75988`. But I do not support it because it just pollutes the commit message with something that has no meaning outside of github. It also works fine if you just put `Fixes #75988` in the PR description.

I missed that point in the guideline.
My bad.
Changed it.
